rationale: The hypothesis is supported by muscle imaging and clinical phenotypic patterns across published cohorts. In sporadic inclusion body myositis (sIBM), deep finger flexor (flexor digitorum profundus, FDP) weakness and fatty infiltration are signature hallmarks, while the sartorius and gracilis muscles are characteristically spared (Cox et al., 2011; Merrison & Brady, 2025). Conversely, in adult-onset and classical SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29), muscle MRI consistently demonstrates prominent, selective fatty degeneration of the sartorius and gracilis muscles (Muelas et al., 2026; Iruzubieta et al., 2024). While adult-onset SNUPN myopathy presents as a phenocopy mimicking IBM due to proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory involvement, SNUPN is not among the recognized causes of prominent finger flexor weakness (Nicolau et al., 2020). However, confidence is tempered because adult-onset SNUPN has only been documented in a single family (n=2 siblings).

evidence.text: Two siblings with adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presented with proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness and early respiratory involvement mimicking inclusion body myositis. Muscle MRI revealed marked selective fatty degeneration in sartorius, gracilis, paravertebral, and triceps brachii muscles.

evidence.text: Finger flexor weakness is a hallmark of sIBM and is documented in specific hereditary myopathies (e.g., ACTA1, CRYAB, DMD, DYSF, FLNC, GAA, GNE, HNRNPDL, LAMA2, MYH7, VCP), but SNUPN is not among the recognized entities causing finger flexor weakness.

source.title: Myopathies with finger flexor weakness: not only inclusion‐body myositis
source.quote: Among these, weakness predominantly affecting finger flexors is an uncommon pattern, most frequently found in sporadic inclusion-body myositis... individual reports and small case series have documented finger flexor weakness in sarcoid and amyloid myopathy, and in inherited myopathies caused by ACTA1, CRYAB, DMD, DYSF, FLNC, GAA, GNE, HNRNPDL, LAMA2, MYH7, and VCP mutations.

conflicts: Extremely limited sample size: adult-onset SNUPN-related myopathy has only been reported in 2 siblings from a single family, meaning specific preservation of forearm deep finger flexors in late-stage disease has not been verified across diverse cohorts.

While Muelas et al. (2026) report that adult-onset SNUPN presents with proximo-distal weakness mimicking inclusion body myositis, detailed MRC scores specifically quantifying flexor digitorum profundus strength relative to intrinsic hand and proximal muscles were not distinguished in the summary data.

new_directions.question_text: Does whole-body and forearm muscle MRI confirm complete sparing of flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus in adult-onset SNUPN patients presenting with distal upper-limb weakness?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether forearm flexor compartment involvement is absent on volumetric T1/STIR MRI will confirm whether finger flexor sparing reliably excludes sIBM phenocopies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the frequency of asymptomatic or subclinical cerebellar atrophy and early respiratory failure in adult-onset myopathy cohorts suspected of having atypical sIBM?
new_directions.rationale: Early respiratory dysfunction and central nervous system signs (e.g., cerebellar atrophy noted in SNUPN) are virtually unheard of in typical sIBM and could serve as earlier clinical discriminators prior to muscle MRI.
